content_preview.summary: ty 0.0.93, released October 28, adds diagnostic baselines as a preview feature, configured through a baseline setting and ty check --update-baseline; the format may change.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

The Python type checker ty, developed in the `astral-sh/ty` repository, released version 0.0.93 on October 28, 2026. According to its [release notes](https://github.com/astral-sh/ty/releases/tag/0.0.93), the release lists diagnostic baselines under "Preview features", described as a way "to help adopt ty in projects with existing errors". Neighbouring releases 0.0.92 (October 26), 0.0.94 (October 28) and 0.0.95 (October 29) each list their own changes.

editor_notes.content_quality: Concise first-party Briefing (417 words, within 300-800). Clear structure, a dedicated 'What Is Not Stated' section, accurate per-release attribution.
editor_notes.source_verification: Read all four snapshots (source-0..3.html.gz; all HTTP 200, suspicious_patterns null for all) and re-fetched each release body live via the GitHub API (published_at 0.0.92 2026-10-26T03:15:04Z; 0.0.93 2026-10-28T00:53:48Z; 0.0.94 2026-10-28T18:07:33Z; 0.0.95 2026-10-29T19:23:48Z; none flagged prerelease, none draft). source-0 (0.0.92): 'Emit SARIF reports with `ty check --output-format sarif`' under CLI; four Django entries under Core type checking (pk/id types, <field>_id, get_<field>_display, get_next_by/get_previous_by) - confirmed; the 0.0.92 notes contain no baseline or startup entry. source-1 (0.0.93): 'Preview features' section with the diagnostic-baseline entry; wording 'help adopt ty in projects with existing errors' matches (article quotes 'to help adopt ty in projects with existing errors' from 'Add diagnostic baselines to help adopt...'; the quoted fragment is verbatim); [tool.ty] baseline = "ty-baseline.json"; `ty check --update-baseline`; 'filter matching diagnostics from CLI output and show them as hints in the language server' verbatim; 'The baseline format may change while the feature is in preview.' verbatim; 'Optimize Linux x86-64 ty releases with LLVM BOLT' verbatim under Performance; fix for narrowing of strings and integers compared with enum members, panic checking truthiness in a loop, hang negating recursive unions - confirmed. source-2 (0.0.94): bug-fix release; 'Fix Linux x86-64 startup on older kernels' verbatim; panics for comprehension filter, diagnostic sorting without source location, chained assignment with missing value - confirmed; no causal link to BOLT or any earlier change is claimed (article explicitly says the notes do not state one). source-3 (0.0.95): six bug fixes and three LSP entries; placing variable type inlay hints after grouping parentheses - confirmed; 0.0.95 is cited only as neighbouring-release context and no 0.0.95 feature is misattributed. The word '(preview)' labelling is the notes' own ('Preview features', 'while the feature is in preview'). 'Python type checker' is stated on the release-page metadata ('Python type checker and language server, written in Rust') in each snapshot; the article does not rely on docs.astral.sh or pypi.org. No contributors are named in the article, so no credit misattribution. All four versions are 0.0.x and the article does not call them stable. github.com is on config/source_allowlist.txt. Independent-source count not applicable (Briefing); all sources are first-party, appropriate for a release report.

'Not stated' claims verified: notes do not give a timeline for leaving preview, VCS guidance, or comparisons with other tools, and none mention Pyrefly (0 hits in all four bodies).
